title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Photoelectric Effect & Observations
points: Photoelectric effect: Phenomenon of emission of electrons (photoelectrons) from a metal surface when light of suitable frequency is incident on it.
Experimental Facts:
(1) Instantaneous emission: Photoelectrons are emitted within ~10⁻⁹ seconds with no detectable time lag.
(2) Threshold frequency (ν₀): Characteristic minimum frequency below which NO emission occurs, regardless of intensity.
(3) Photocurrent is directly proportional to intensity of incident radiation (I ∝ Intensity) at constant frequency.
(4) Maximum kinetic energy (KE_max) and stopping potential (V₀) depend linearly on frequency ν, and are completely independent of intensity.

nodes.title: Failure of Wave Theory of Light
points: Classical Wave Theory failed because:

(1) Energy distribution: Wave theory predicts energy is distributed uniformly over wavefront. Low-intensity light should require hours/days for an electron to accumulate enough escape energy, contradicting instantaneous emission (< 10⁻⁹ s).
(2) Threshold frequency: Wave theory predicts high enough intensity of ANY frequency should eject electrons, failing to explain existence of threshold frequency ν₀.

(3) Kinetic energy: Wave theory predicts larger intensity (larger electric field amplitude) should give higher kinetic energy, contradicting experimental observation that KE depends ONLY on frequency.

formulas.label: Wave theory discrepancy
formulas.expr: Predicted: KE ∝ Intensity (Wrong!) | Actual: KE ∝ Frequency

nodes.title: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation & Work Function
points: Einstein proposed that radiation travels as localized packets of energy called Photons (or Quanta), each of energy E = hν.
Work Function (Φ₀): Minimum energy required to liberate an electron from metal surface: Φ₀ = h ν₀ = h c / λ₀ (SI unit: eV or J; 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J).
Einstein's Photoelectric Equation: Energy of photon = Work function + Maximum KE of emitted electron.
KE_max = h ν − Φ₀ = h (ν − ν₀) = h c (1/λ − 1/λ₀).
In terms of Stopping Potential V₀: e V₀ = h ν − Φ₀ ⟹ V₀ = (h/e) ν − (Φ₀/e).

nodes.title: Characteristics of Photons
points: Photons travel at the speed of light in vacuum: c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
Energy of a photon: E = hν = hc / λ. Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s. Dimensions: [M¹L²T⁻¹] (same as angular momentum).
Linear momentum of a photon: p = E / c = h / λ.
Rest mass of a photon is strictly ZERO (m₀ = 0). It cannot exist at rest.
Equivalent dynamic mass: m = E / c² = hν / c² = h / (cλ).
Photons are electrically NEUTRAL; they are not deflected by electric or magnetic fields.
In photon-particle collision, total energy and total momentum are conserved, but number of photons may not be conserved.

nodes.title: Photoelectric Graphs & Slopes
points: Graph 1: V₀ vs Frequency ν: A straight line with slope = h/e (universal constant, same for ALL metals!) and x-intercept = ν₀ (threshold frequency). y-intercept = −Φ₀/e.
Graph 2: Photocurrent vs Collector Potential for different intensities at same frequency: Same stopping potential V₀, but higher saturation current for higher intensity.
Graph 3: Photocurrent vs Collector Potential for different frequencies at same intensity: Different stopping potentials (higher ν gives more negative V₀), same saturation current.
Graph 4: Photocurrent vs Intensity: A straight line passing through origin.

nodes.title: de Broglie Hypothesis & Matter Waves
points: de Broglie Hypothesis: A moving material particle possesses wave-like properties (matter waves / de Broglie waves). Nature loves symmetry.
de Broglie wavelength: λ = h / p = h / (m v).
In terms of Kinetic Energy E: p = √(2mE) ⟹ λ = h / √(2mE).
For a gas molecule at absolute temperature T: Average thermal KE E = 3/2 k_B T ⟹ λ = h / √(3 m k_B T).
Matter waves are not electromagnetic waves; they are probability waves representing the probability of finding a particle in space.

nodes.title: de Broglie Wavelength of Accelerated Particles
points: When a charged particle of charge q and mass m is accelerated from rest through potential difference V: KE = q V.
Formula: λ = h / √(2mqV).
For an Electron (m = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C): λ = 1.228 / √V nm = 12.28 / √V Å.
For a Proton (m_p): λ_p = 0.286 / √V Å.
For a Deuteron (m_d = 2m_p, q_d = e): λ_d = 0.202 / √V Å.
For an Alpha particle (m_α = 4m_p, q_α = 2e): λ_α = 0.101 / √V Å.

nodes.title: Davisson-Germer Experiment & Wave Confirmation
points: Davisson and Germer experimentally confirmed the wave nature of electrons through electron diffraction by a nickel crystal.
Key Observation: A sharp peak in scattered electron intensity occurred at accelerating voltage V = 54 V and scattering angle ϕ = 50°.
Bragg's grazing angle: θ = 90° − ϕ/2 = 90° − 25° = 65°. For Nickel lattice spacing d = 0.091 nm.
Bragg's law: λ = 2d sinθ = 2 × 0.091 × sin 65° = 0.165 nm.
de Broglie theoretical formula: λ = 1.228 / √54 nm = 0.167 nm.
The striking agreement between experimental (0.165 nm) and theoretical (0.167 nm) values definitively proved de Broglie's matter wave hypothesis.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Questions & Derivations
points: Board Favourite #1: State Einstein's photoelectric equation and explain all characteristics of photoelectric effect using it.
Board Favourite #2: Define: (1) Threshold frequency, (2) Threshold wavelength, (3) Work function, (4) Stopping potential.
Board Favourite #3: Derive expression for de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential difference V.
Board Favourite #4: Describe Davisson and Germer experiment with neat schematic diagram and explain how it proved wave nature of electrons.
Board Favourite #5: Sketch and explain the graph of stopping potential versus frequency of incident radiation.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, hc Value Hacks & Exam Traps
points: Calculation Hack: hc ≈ 1242 eV·nm ≈ 12400 eV·Å. Energy of photon in eV: E(eV) = 1242 / λ(nm) = 12400 / λ(Å).
Universal Slope Trap: The slope of the V₀ vs ν graph is ALWAYS h/e = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ V·s, which is identical for ALL metals (Cs, Na, K, Pt, etc.)!

Intensity vs Frequency Trap: Doubling intensity DOUBLES the photocurrent and saturation current, but KE_max and V₀ remain UNCHANGED. Doubling frequency increases KE_max and V₀, but photocurrent remains unchanged.
Threshold Wavelength Trap: Photoelectric emission occurs when λ ≤ λ₀ (wavelength must be LESS than or equal to threshold wavelength).
Ratio of de Broglie Wavelengths: For same accelerating voltage V: λ_e : λ_p : λ_d : λ_α = 1/√(m_e q_e) : 1/√(m_p q_p) : 1/√(m_d q_d) : 1/√(m_α q_α).

formulas.label: Universal slope
formulas.expr: Slope = h / e (same for all metals)
